note: Held-out CrowS-Pairs test split (n=905), Gemma-2-2B + Gemma Scope SAE (JumpReLU, layer 24/26, width 16k, avg_l0_38). Baseline vs encoder-SAE steering (alpha=2.0, tau=0.0, topk=32).
conclusion: Encoder-SAE steering beats decoder ablation and direct-activation steering on genuinely held-out data using an independently-trained SAE (Gemma Scope, JumpReLU) on a second model family. Effect is significant under both the unpaired z-test (unlike Phi-3, which needed the paired correction) and the paired McNemar test, at a much smaller p-value than Phi-3's replication.
